newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain urges France to maintain anti-terror resolve.
newsitem.headline: Spain urges France to maintain anti-terror resolve.

text.p: Spain on Monday urged the new left-wing French government to maintain close cooperation in combatting terrorism.
"The anti-terrorist battle must be and is separate from ideologies and from partisan debates of left and right," Spanish Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told reporters.

The minister said he was confident the "exemplary" cooperation between centre-right governments in France and Spain before Sunday's French election would continue under a Socialist-led coalition in Paris.

Spain's year-old conservative government has repeatedly expressed its satisfaction with a tougher French attitude towards the Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA over the past year. ETA has a strong power base in southern France.

Both government and Socialist opposition figures called for the new French government to put a speedy end to attacks on Spanish trucks carrying fruit and vegetables by French farmers demanding tighter control on cheaper imported produce.

"Now that the election campaign is over, it is hoped the new government will be completely serious in ending the embarrassing attacks suffered by Spanish transporters," said chief Foreign Ministry spokesman Inocencio Arias.
